honest_c3: C1 sentinel marker pattern (__ANIMA_EEG_FAIL__) is anima-internal convention; no industry standard for EEG protocol error contracts (closest: BIDS log JSON, but BIDS does not specify a stderr trailer).
C2 say_cue is macOS-only ($1-Yuna voice locale-dependent); on linux/RunPod pods say is absent so cue silently no-ops; sentinel trailer still emits independently.

C3 hexa stage1 has no closures / no fn-typed params, so the BG-spec example safe_call(label, fn) is reframed as safe_call(label, rc) — rc-passthrough rather than lambda-wrap. Functional equivalent, no semantic loss.
C4 Retroactive cost — 7 priority protocols × ~5 sentinel emit sites each ≈ 35 patches; this BG lands berger_session_audio.hexa only (witness case), spec-binds the other 6 for next cycle.
C5 KIND enum churn — 9 entries today; expect 2-3/quarter additions as new fail modes surface. AI parser MUST treat unknown KIND as OTHER, not crash.

C6 chicken-egg — if _lib_safe_call.hexa itself fails to load, no sentinel is emitted because the wrapper is the fault. Mitigation: protocols inline the minimal emit fns (ai_emit_fail / ai_emit_ok) so the contract holds even if the lib import fails.

C7 stderr ordering — interleaved subprocess stderr (BrainFlow Python) may insert lines between trailer lines; AI parser MUST anchor on __ANIMA_EEG_FAIL__ then look forward (≤20 lines) for reason: / voice_emitted:.

C8 hexa runtime exit-code clamp — observed --bogus-flag returns rc=0 from `hexa run` even though the protocol returns 2; this is a pre-existing hexa stage1 quirk (sibling BG-HEXA-LANG fix territory). The sentinel emit still surfaces the fault correctly to the AI agent via stderr trailer; the rc-based exit signal is currently unreliable, so AI agents SHOULD prefer the trailer over rc.
